key_insight: Photon-correlation measurements on Yb3+-doped CsPbCl3 do not support quantum cutting; instead, they show anti-bunching consistent with Auger quenching.
engineering_relevance: Claims of >100% photoluminescence quantum yield in Yb3+-doped lead-halide perovskites may not translate into reliable photon-multiplying performance for photovoltaic spectral conversion.
method: Performed photon-correlation analysis on CsPbCl3:Yb3+ nanocrystals and bulk samples.
Tested the expected photon bunching signature of quantum-cutting emission.
Compared observed emission statistics with the known Auger-quenching pathway.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports no photon bunching; instead, the measured emission under focused excitation shows anti-bunching, contradicting the quantum-cutting expectation.
watch_item: These results question the quantum-cutting interpretation in CsPb(Cl1-xBrx)3:Yb3+, so device designs should not assume >100% PLQY implies true photon doubling.
paper_title: Photon Statistics from Yb3+-Doped CsPbCl3 are Inconsistent with Quantum Cutting
